_comment: Role -> model seat. Each model family maps to the CLI that runs it (`clis`): anthropic seats run as headless Claude Code (`claude -p`), openai seats as headless Codex (`codex exec`), google seats as headless Antigravity (`agy -p`). There are no fallback models. Model changes happen only through `pipeline trial`; vendor benchmarks nominate, never decide. `pipeline render-agents` regenerates the Claude Code agent files from this registry and the suite diffs them (drift guard).

interactive.purpose: The one agent the operator talks to. Routes every ask into quick or plan; never does the work itself.

history.why: DECISION interactive-fallback: operator chose glm-5.3 as the manual standard-tier fallback for the interactive seat when the premium allowance is hit; to be revisited by trial-report interactive

DECISION no-premium-seats: the registry never seats a premium model in any field, including interactive; glm-5.3 (the operator's stated preference) becomes the interim primary until trial-report interactive names the measured best standard-tier arm.
parity 9: interactive seat guard - write tools refused; the seat routes work through run/quick dispatches; the role prompt carries the receipt naming the dispatch it should have used

DECISION benchmark-update (2026-11-03): gpt-6.1-sol is AA 55 max / 50 high (vs gpt-6-sol 48/43), now the #1 standard-tier model; full evidence in docs/model-selection/UPDATE-LATEST.md. For the interactive fallback swap: gpt-6.1-sol at low effort gives AA 35 with TTFT 2.51s at $0.16/task, replacing claude-sonnet-5 as the conversational fallback per the same UPDATE-LATEST.md analysis.

DECISION interactive-kimi (2026-11-03, operator directed): operator wants the smartest Chinese frontier for the interactive seat; kimi-k3.1-pro is AA 46 vs GLM-5.3 AA 32 (+14), TTFT 3.45s within the 5s conversational fence, $3.68/task vs $5.01; trade-off accepted: 32 t/s vs GLM 90 t/s streaming. Collision status: no other seat currently uses a moonshot model (reviewer-c moved kimi-k3 -> claude-sonnet-5-5 on 2026-09-29; reviewers are openai/xai/anthropic), so there is no cross-seat collision; quota_fallback set to gpt-6.1-sol@high because same-family kimi is illegal. Evidence: docs/model-selection/UPDATE-LATEST.md.

DECISION leave-devpass (2026-11-07): operator cancelled DevPass and moved to a Claude subscription (Claude Code) plus Codex. Anthropic seats run on `claude -p`; the single sealed reviewer runs on `codex exec`. Fallback and quota_fallback arms are removed; reviewer-a/b/c collapse into one reviewer.

DECISION operator-seats (2026-11-09): operator moved the interactive seat to Claude Fable 5.2 directly, outside pipeline trial. Verified the model id runs on this account; no published benchmarks for Fable 5.2 yet.

DECISION operator-seats (2026-11-12): operator set the interactive seat to medium effort. Published benchmark (Artificial Analysis, 2026-11-10): Fable 5.2 medium scores 56 at 8.3 min and $3.80 per task, above the previous Opus 5.5 high (52, 9.5 min, $3.46); Fable 5.2 high scores 62 at 17.7 min and $9.08. In the operator's own interactive sessions Fable 5.2 high had a median turn of 38 s (p90 180 s) against 24 s (p90 79 s) for Opus 5.5 high, with 42% of output spent thinking.

DECISION cost-swap implementer->terra (2026-09-07, operator-approved): measured journal spend showed claude-sonnet-5 at 58% of all estate cost ($127.71 of $221.12 across 328 dispatches), with 34 of its 75 implementer dispatches not landing ok (the timeout class). gpt-5.6-terra@high is published-cheaper by 4.1x ($0.81 vs $3.31/task blended; $1.75/$7.00 vs $2.00/$10.00 per M in/out, gateway pricing) with comparable-or-better evidence: AA Intelligence 47 vs 45, LiveBench code_completion 80.4 vs 78.3, typescript 46.7 vs 50.0 (sonnet slightly ahead), code_generation 76.1 vs 83.1 (sonnet's edge, from-scratch work; the implementer role here is mostly completing/fixing code). Sources: artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models and livebench.ai/table_2026_06_25.csv, both retrieved 2026-09-05, in docs/model-selection/SEAT-EVIDENCE.md. Same swap applied to frontend-worker (same seat, zero dispatches so far, identical criteria). Sonnet-5 remains seated as interactive-fallback and reviewer fallbacks; the from-scratch codegen edge is noted and re-checkable via pipeline trial if implementer quality regresses.

history.why: DECISION fallback-sweep (2026-09-06, completed by the interactor after two worker timeouts left the analysis unfinished): criterion = same as the primary's. For researcher/document-writer (reading/digesting, prose) the published numbers rank glm-5.3 above claude-sonnet-5 on every axis of the role's criterion: LiveBench summarize 74.55 vs 71.22, AA intelligence 49 vs 45, TTFT 2.0s vs 2.9s (sources: artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models, livebench.ai/table_2026_06_25.csv, both retrieved 2026-09-05, in docs/model-selection/SEAT-EVIDENCE.md). kimi-k3's AA 50 is beaten here by its LB summarize 69.35 (below sonnet's 71.22) and TTFT 28.5s. Interactive KEEPS claude-sonnet-5: conversational TTFT 2.9s beats kimi-k3's 28.5s; glm-5.3 is unusable as its own fallback (same model as the primary). No other seat's fallback changed: each current one already wins its role's criterion (implementer gpt-5.6-luna on code speed/cost, reviewers deepseek-v4-pro/gpt-5.3-codex/gemini-3.8-flash on intelligence+TTFT).

DECISION fallback-refresh (2026-11-03, operator directed): glm-5.3 was seated on 2026-09-05 fallback-sweep numbers that have since been renormed twice to AA 32; grok-4-6 prose avg 72.7 (summarize 68.1, story 78.3, paraphrase 71.8) beats glm-5.3 approx 70.5, freed from seats since grok-4-7 took reviewer-b (no collision with any seat primary or other fallback), xai family distinct from google primary. Note: reviewer-b primary is grok-4-7 (xai family), which overlaps this fallback's family but is NOT a collision-rule violation (the rule is per-role fallback-differs-from-own-primary). quota_fallback also corrected from the fall-to-self gemini-3.8-flash to grok-4-6@high. Evidence: docs/model-selection/UPDATE-LATEST.md.

DECISION fallback-grok-4-7 (2026-11-03, operator directed): audit confirmed grok-4-6 was the only seat subordinating quality to avoid cross-seat collision; the rest of the board shares models across seats freely, so the operator standardized on quality-first. grok-4-7 prose composite 77.05 beats grok-4-6 approx 72.7 (evidence: docs/model-selection/UPDATE-LATEST.md document-writer verdict). Collision note: grok-4-7 is reviewer-b primary; operator accepts the coupling, consistent with the rest of the board.
